title: SmartAgri DTPB FTP UGM Research Team Participates in the 2026 RGBI Proposal Presentation Selection
author: Fahmi Arsyad
excerpt: Smartagri UGM researchers participated in the 2026 Bank Indonesia Research Grant (RGBI) proposal presentation selection, hosted online by Bank Indonesia Institute (BINS) on April 20, presenting an IoT-based precision agriculture proposal addressing climate change adaptation and food security. The session was attended by community farming partners (KWT) and an international collaborator from Kyushu University, Japan, reflecting the study's multi-stakeholder and global research dimension.
body:
**Yogyakarta, April 20, 2026.** Researchers from the Smart Agriculture Research Center (Smartagri), Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (DTPB), Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (FTP UGM), participated in the 2026 Research Grant Bank Indonesia (RGBI) Proposal Presentation Selection, organized online by Bank Indonesia Institute (BINS). This activity is one of the stages in the research proposal evaluation process aimed at producing scientific contributions to strategic national issues, particularly in the area of food security.

The presentation selection was held on Monday, April 20, 2026, via Zoom Meeting. It was attended by researchers from various institutions who had passed the administrative screening and were formally invited by the RGBI Management Team. During the event, the Smartagri research team presented a research proposal on agricultural technology innovation in addressing climate change challenges. In general, the proposed research examines the use of Internet of Things (IoT)-based technology to improve agricultural production efficiency and productivity, as well as evaluating its economic impact on local food systems. The research approach was designed using a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods to produce comprehensive, data-driven analysis.

![](/brand/uploads/20-4-2.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/20-4-3.webp)

The event was also attended by representatives of the Women Farmers Group (Kelompok Wanita Tani/KWT) as program partners responsible for the implementation and community-scale testing of the technology, as well as Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D. from Kyushu University, Japan, as an international research collaborator providing a global perspective on the development of precision agriculture technology and sensor-based systems.

During the presentation and discussion sessions, the research team emphasized the importance of integrating precision agriculture technology as part of a climate change adaptation strategy. The proposed innovations are oriented not only toward increasing production yields, but also toward improving the efficiency of resource use (including water, fertilizers, and labor) and their contribution to food price stability.

The participation of Smartagri DTPB FTP UGM in the 2026 RGBI selection demonstrates its commitment to developing applied research with direct impact on communities and policymakers. This involvement simultaneously strengthens Smartagri's role as a center of excellence in the development of precision agriculture technology and biosystems that are adaptive to global challenges.

This activity is aligned with the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly **SDG 2** _(Zero Hunger)_, **SDG 9** _(Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure)_, and **SDG 13** _(Climate Action)_, through the development of efficient, adaptive, and sustainable agricultural technology innovations. Through participation in the RGBI 2026 program, Smartagri DTPB FTP UGM is expected to continue contributing to the development of research-based solutions that support national food security and Indonesia's economic stability.
